question: Who could receive communion, and how often?

answers.label: Only the baptized who hold the faith and live by it
Every Lord's day, and for some daily
At least once a year, at Easter

overview.text: Only the baptized received: the Didache and Justin say so plainly, and Justin adds right faith and a Christian life.
All present received every Sunday, and deacons took it to the absent. Tertullian says Christians received at dawn gatherings too.
As lay communion grew rare, the Fourth Lateran Council (1215) required at least once a year, at Easter.

quotes.author: Didache
quotes.english: Let no one eat or drink of your Eucharist except those baptized in the name of the Lord. For about this too the Lord said: "Do not give what is holy to the dogs" (Matthew 7:6).
quotes.original: μηδεὶς δὲ φαγέτω μηδὲ πιέτω ἀπὸ τῆς εὐχαριστίας ὑμῶν, ἀλλ’ οἱ βαπτισθέντες εἰς ὄνομα κυρίου: καὶ γὰρ περὶ τούτου εἴρηκεν ὁ κύριος: Μὴ δῶτε τὸ ἄγιον τοῖς κυσί.
quotes.context: Communion was for the baptized from the first.

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: This food is called among us Eucharist, of which no one may partake except one who believes that what we teach is true, and has been washed with the washing for forgiveness of sins and rebirth, and lives as Christ handed down.
quotes.original: Καὶ ἡ τροφὴ αὕτη καλεῖται παρ᾿ ἡ μῖν εὐχαριστία, ἧς οὐδενὶ ἄλλῳ μετασχεῖν ἐξόν ἐστιν ἢ τῷ πιστεύοντι ἀληθῆ εἶναι τὰ δεδιδαγμένα ὑφ᾿ ἡμῶν, καὶ λουσαμένῳ τὸ ὑπὲρ ἀφέσεως ἁμαρτιῶν καὶ εἰς ἀναγέννησιν λουτρόν, καὶ οὕτως βιοῦντι ὡς ὁ Χριστὸς παρέδωκεν.
quotes.context: Three conditions: right faith, baptism, a Christian life.

quotes.author: Justin Martyr
quotes.english: ... and the distribution and sharing of the things over which thanks has been given is made to each, and to those not present it is sent through the deacons.
quotes.original: καὶ ἡ διάδοσις καὶ ἡ μετάληψις ἀπὸ τῶν εὐχαριστηθέντων ἑκάστῳ γίνεται, καὶ τοῖς οὐ παροῦσι διὰ τῶν διακόνων πέμπεται.
quotes.context: Every Sunday, everyone present received, and the absent were sent their share.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: The sacrament of the Eucharist, which the Lord commanded to be taken at mealtime and by all, we take even in gatherings before dawn, and from the hand of none but those who preside.
quotes.original: Eucharistiae sacramentum et in tempore victus et omnibus mandatum a domino, etiam antelucanis coetibus nec de aliorum manu quam praesidentium sumimus.
quotes.context: Tertullian elsewhere speaks of Christians taking the sacrament at home before other food (To His Wife 2.5).

quotes.author: John Chrysostom
quotes.english: I see many partaking of the body of Christ carelessly and as chance has it, and from habit and custom rather than from thought and consideration. If the season of holy Lent comes on, whoever one may be, he partakes of the mysteries; if the day of Epiphany comes on. ... In the other seasons, though often pure, you do not come; but at Pascha, though you have ventured something, you come. O the habit! O the presumption! In vain the daily sacrifice, in vain we have stood at the altar: no one partakes.
quotes.original: Πολλοὺς ὁρῶ τοὺς σώματος τοῦ Χριστοῦ μετέχοντας ἁπλῶς καὶ ὡς ἔτυχε, καὶ συνηθείᾳ μᾶλλον καὶ νόμῳ, ἢ λογισμῷ καὶ διανοίᾳ. Ἂν ἐπιστῇ, φησὶν, ὁ τῆς ἁγίας Τεσσαρακοστῆς καιρὸς, οἷος ἐὰν ᾖ τις, μετέχει τῶν μυστηρίων, ἂν ἐπιστῇ ἡ τῶν Ἐπιφανίων ἡμέρα. ... Ἐν μὲν τοῖς ἄλλοις καιροῖς οὐδὲ καθαροὶ πολλάκις ὄντες προσέρχεσθε, ἐν δὲ τῷ Πάσχα, κἂν ᾖ τι τετολμημένον ὑμῖν, πρόσιτε. Ὢ τῆς συνηθείας! ὢ τῆς προλήψεως! εἰκῆ θυσία καθημερινὴ, εἰκῆ παρεστήκαμεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, οὐδεὶς ὁ μετέχων.
quotes.context: The passage is Homily 3, subdivision 4, on Ephesians; in the library's PG-chunked sections it is section 4.6 (PG 62.28 to 29), because the section numbers run one ahead of the homily numbers. Chrysostom's own rule, stated just before, is that purity of soul, not a feast day, makes a person fit to come. The answer tags the practice he is rebuking, festival-only communion, not his prescription.

quotes.author: Fourth Lateran Council
quotes.english: Every believer of either sex, after reaching the age of discretion, shall faithfully confess all his sins alone to his own priest at least once a year, ... receiving reverently at least at Easter the sacrament of the Eucharist, unless by his own priest's counsel he abstains for a time for some reasonable cause.
quotes.original: Omnis utriusque sexus fidelis, postquam ad annos discretionis pervenerit, omnia sua solus peccata saltem semel in anno fideliter confiteatur proprio sacerdoti ... suscipiens reverenter ad minus in Pascha Eucharistiae sacramentum , nisi forte de consilio proprii sacerdotis ob aliquam rationabilem causam ad tempus ab eius perceptione duxerit abstinendum
quotes.context: By the Middle Ages most lay people received rarely, so the council set a minimum.

gaps.author: Augustine of Hippo
gaps.why: Some receive daily, some on certain days; follow your church's custom.
